prerequisites: Basic mathematical knowledge as foreseen by the curricula of secondary schools.

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and understanding of basic notions, constructions, and results of linear algebra and geometry, as indicated in the course program.
Ability to solve basic exercises in linear algebra and geometry.
Ability to apply the demonstrative techniques seen in class to solve problems in linear algebra and geometry.
Ability to critically evaluate the result of a problem.
Ability to logically present demonstrations in linear algebra and geometry.

syllabus_topics: Preliminaries, vector spaces (definition and properties), vector subspaces (definition and properties), generators and generated spaces, linear independence, bases, coordinates. Examples.

Linear mappings (definition and examples); kernel and image, rank-nullity theorem. Matrix representation, matrix algebra, change of basis. Rank of a matrix. Linear systems, Rouché-Capelli theorem and solution space of a system.
Eigenvalues and eigenvectors. Diagonalization. Spectral theorem for symmetric operators.

Analytic geometry of the plane and space: lines and planes in parametric and Cartesian form, notions of parallelism, incidence, and orthogonality. Conics (canonical forms and reduction to canonical form).
assessment_rules: The final exam includes a written and an oral test, aiming to evaluate the learning of basic notions and the ability to use them for solving basic geometric problems. The evaluation ranges from 'Insufficient' for severe conceptual errors to 'Excellent or outstanding' (29-30 cum laude) for complete, in-depth knowledge and critical thinking. 'La Lode' (cum laude) is awarded for brilliant and original work.
bibliography: Any basic linear algebra textbook will be fine. For example: Enrico Schlesinger "Algebra Lineare e Geometria" Zanichelli
